item.title: Backups
item.description: Backups # Econumo has no built-in backup mechanism, so setting up backups for your instance is up to you. By default Econumo keeps all its data in a single SQLite file, which makes backups easy. In the Docker setup that file is in the db volume, at /app/var/db/db.sqlite (the path in your DATABASEURL). With the single binary it is wherever your DATABASEURL points, /var/lib/econumo/db.sqlite in the example setup. The database

item.title: CLI (terminal) commands
item.description: CLI (terminal) commands # Econumo ships as a single binary driven by subcommands. serve runs the server, and the resource:action commands handle management. In the Docker image the binary is /app/econumo, so you run commands with docker compose exec: docker compose exec econumo /app/econumo [args] With the single binary, run commands as the service user, with the environment file loaded the same way systemd loads it for the service: sudo

item.title: Configuration
item.description: Configuration # Econumo is configured entirely through environment variables. There is no admin screen. With Docker they go in .env. With the single binary they go in /etc/econumo/env (see Installation). After a change, apply it with docker compose up -d, which recreates the container (docker compose restart keeps the old values), or with sudo systemctl restart econumo. The repository has two templates: .env.example holds the settings most setups need. docs/full.env.example

item.title: Debug Econumo
item.description: Overview # Econumo uses these HTTP response codes: 1. HTTP 2xx: everything is fine. 2. HTTP 4xx: a problem with the user's input. 3. HTTP 5xx: a server error. Every response also carries an X-Request-Id header (a UUID). Include it when you report a problem: it finds the exact request in the logs. In this section # Is the server up? item.title: Installation
item.description: Installation # Econumo is a single, self-contained Go binary. It serves both the API and the web app, runs database migrations by itself on every start, and stores data in SQLite by default (PostgreSQL is also supported). item.title: Multi-Currency support
item.description: Multi-Currency Support # Econumo works with any number of currencies. On a self-hosted instance you decide which currencies the server offers, and where the exchange rates come from. There are two kinds of currencies: Global currencies are available to everyone on the instance. You add them from the command line, and their rates come from Open Exchange Rates. Custom currencies belong to one user, who creates them under Settings →

item.title: Single sign-on
item.description: Single sign-on # Econumo can add Sign in with Google, Sign in with Apple and a button for your own OpenID Connect provider (Authentik, Keycloak, Zitadel, Okta, Cloudflare Access, …) to the sign-in and sign-up pages. Buttons can sit next to email and password, or replace them. Each provider is an optional slot, configured only through environment variables. You can enable all three at once. Most self-hosted instances enable one.
